newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar ends little changed in choppy trade.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar ends little changed in choppy trade.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed little changed on Tuesday in choppy trade, as late Asian selling brought it sharply back from its highs.
The Kiwi was ending the day around US$0.7055/62, unchanged from its opening level, while nudging up to 67.58 on its Trade-Weighted Index from 67.51.

Dealers said the currency was looking heavy after exhausting a good run at the topside which carried it up to a high of 0.7093. Asian selling slapped it down in afternoon trade, but they said it could still be poised for a retest of 71 cents. "You have to expect in the medium-term the Kiwi's going to
continue to be attractive and to appreciate," an Auckland dealer said, adding New Zealand yield differentials were still attractive to offshore investors.

He said there was a natural imbalance in the market, with strong exporter demand and little supply. "I would imagine that some time in the next day or two we will try and get towards 71, and there's a reasonable chance we will get up through that."
He said the Reserve Bank may be concerned that the fall in 90-day bank bill rates, now at 8.90 percent, was overdone, and may favour a fraction more strength in the TWI to compensate.
A Wellington dealer said there was still talk of more eurokiwi and samurai bond issues, which should keep the currency underpinned.

Balanced against that was ongoing political uncertainty, with nationalist New Zealand First entering a fresh round of coalition talks with Labour late Tuesday and planning more meetings in coming days with both Labour and the caretaker National party government.
NZ First holds the balance of power after an inconclusive general election on October 12.
